extracted.intended_audience: state, local, tribal, territorial, and federal emergency management personnel and trainers (NIMS/ICS)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the National Incident Management System (NIMS) core curriculum and associated Incident Command System (ICS) and Emergency Operations Center (EOC) courses intended to train personnel to implement NIMS principles and perform ICS/EOC roles. Includes baseline, additional, and position-specific course objectives and instructional methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS Training Program — core curriculum adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIMS Training Program identifies courses critical to train personnel capable of implementing all functions of emergency management and establishes the NIMS core curriculum to ensure it adequately trains emergency and incident response personnel to all concepts and principles of each NIMS component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's purpose is to provide a consistent curriculum that adequately covers all concepts and principles across NIMS components so government, private-sector, and nongovernmental organizations can work together during domestic incidents. (Reference: link to NIMS Training Program document.)

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-700 NIMS, an Introduction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This independent study course provides the foundation for understanding NIMS as a consistent nationwide template to enable all government, private-sector, and nongovernmental organizations to work together during domestic incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS-100 Introduction to the Incident Command System
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces ICS and provides the foundation for higher level ICS training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course describes the history, features and principles, and organizational structure of ICS and explains the relationship between ICS and NIMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS-200 Basic Incident Command System for Initial Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Enables personnel to operate efficiently during an incident or event within the ICS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to provide training and resources for personnel likely to assume a supervisory position within ICS; focuses on initial response functions and supervisory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-800 National Response Framework (NRF), an Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces participants to the concepts and principles of the National Response Framework (NRF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent study course presenting NRF fundamentals and how it integrates with NIMS and incident response.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS-300 Intermediate ICS for Expanding Incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides training and resources for personnel who require advanced knowledge and application of ICS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands upon information covered in ICS-100 and ICS-200 to prepare personnel for managing expanding incidents and more complex ICS functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS-400 Advanced ICS
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides training and resources for personnel who require advanced application of ICS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Builds on ICS-100 through ICS-300 to develop advanced application skills for large or complex incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-specific training for Command and General Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses designed to provide State and local-level emergency responders with a robust understanding of the duties, responsibilities, and capabilities of Command and General Staff members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional approaches include exercises, simulations, discussions, and a final exam to enable participants to process and apply new knowledge. Example position-specific courses listed: E/L 950 (Incident Commander), E/L 952 (Public Information Officer), E/L 954 (Safety Officer), E/L 956 (Liaison Officer), E/L 958 (Operations Section Chief), E/L 960 (Division/Group Supervisor), E/L 962 (Planning Section Chief), E/L 964 (Situation Unit Leader), E/L 965 (Resources Unit Leader), E/L 967 (Logistics Section Chief), E/L 969 (Communications Unit Leader), E/L 970 (Supply Unit Leader), E/L 971 (Facilities Unit Leader), E/L 973 (Finance/Admin. Section Chief), E/L 975 (Finance/Admin. Unit Leader).

rubrics_metrics.name: EOC training — overview of key NIMS principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses present an overview of key NIMS principles relating to Multi-Agency Coordination Systems (MACS), public information, resource management, mutual aid, and communication and information management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EOC-focused training emphasizes how NIMS principles apply to coordination centers and the functional areas necessary for multi-agency coordination during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-706 NIMS Interstate Mutual Aid, an Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides an introduction to NIMS interstate mutual aid and assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants learn about the purpose and benefits of mutual aid and assistance and the emphasis NIMS places on mutual aid and assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-2200 Basic Emergency Operations Center Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces the role, design, and function of the Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and its supportive relationship as a NIMS Command and Coordination component of the Multi-Agency Coordination System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course content focuses on EOC purpose, structure, and how it supports incident management teams within the multi-agency coordination context.

rubrics_metrics.name: G-191 Incident Command System/Emergency Operations Center Interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews ICS and EOC responsibilities and functions and emphasizes the interface between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies heavily on exercises and group discussions to formulate the interface and provides an opportunity for participants to begin developing an interface between an Incident Management Team and EOC personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: E/L/G 2300 Intermediate Emergency Operations Center Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediate course designed to develop deeper EOC capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to: (1) examine the role, design, and function of the EOC and its supportive relationship as a NIMS Command and Coordination component; (2) provide training on staffing, organization, information systems, communications, and equipment needs at the EOC (including activating/deactivating and operations), as well as training and exercising; and (3) focus on the role of the EOC as one of four NIMS Command and Coordination functional groups.
